Jonathan Kuminga is a professional basketball player.
Jonathan Kuminga was born on October 6, 2002.
Jonathan Kuminga is Congolese.
The Golden State Warriors are Jonathan Kuminga's current team.
The National Basketball Association (NBA) is the league where Jonathan Kuminga plays.
Jonathan Kuminga chose to forgo his college eligibility and reclassify to the 2020 class to join the NBA G League Ignite.
Kuminga played high school basketball at The Patrick School in Hillside, New Jersey.
The Warriors selected Kuminga with the seventh overall pick in the 2021 NBA draft.
During his rookie season, Kuminga won an NBA championship with the team.
Kuminga began playing basketball in the Democratic Republic of the Congo at age two.
In 2016, Kuminga moved to the U.S. to play high school basketball.
As a freshman, Kuminga played for Huntington Prep School in Huntington, West Virginia.
For his sophomore season, Kuminga transferred to Our Savior New American School in Centereach, New York.
During his sophomore season, Kuminga averaged 25 points, five rebounds, and five assists per game.
In January 2019, Kuminga was named most valuable player of the Slam Dunk to the Beach showcase after scoring 40 points.
Kuminga earned MaxPreps National Sophomore of the Year honors in 2019.
After the season, Kuminga averaged 20.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game for the NY Rens at the Nike Elite Youth Basketball League.
In a game against the Texas Titans, Kuminga scored 43 points, shooting 7 of 11 from three-point range.
Cade Cunningham and Greg Brown were on the team that featured top recruits in the Texas Titans.
For his junior season, Kuminga transferred to The Patrick School in Hillside, New Jersey.
On December 23, 2019, Kuminga made his season debut at The Patrick School after being ruled ineligible for 30 days due to transfer rules.
On January 3, 2020, Kuminga suffered an ankle sprain that sidelined him for about a month.
As a junior, Kuminga averaged 16.2 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game.
Kuminga was considered one of the best recruits in the 2021 class by most recruiting services.
On July 15, 2020, Kuminga reclassified to the 2020 class and announced he would bypass college basketball to join the NBA G League Ignite over offers from Texas Tech, Auburn, Duke, and Kentucky.
At the end of his high school career, Kuminga was a consensus five-star recruit and the best small forward in the 2020 class.
Kuminga was considered the third-best player in his class by Rivals.com and the fourth best by 247Sports.com and ESPN after reclassifying.
On July 15, 2020, Kuminga signed a one-year contract with the NBA G League Ignite.
On February 10, 2021, Kuminga made his debut for the NBA G League Ignite, recording 19 points, four assists and four rebounds in a win over the Santa Cruz Warriors.
Kuminga averaged 15.8 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game during his time with the NBA G League Ignite.
The Golden State Warriors drafted Kuminga as the 7th pick in the 2021 NBA draft.
On August 3, 2021, Kuminga signed with the Golden State Warriors.
On October 30, 2021, Kuminga made his NBA debut, putting up three points and one steal in a 103–82 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder.
On December 18, 2021, Kuminga had his first career start, scoring a then-career-high 26 points in a 119–100 loss to the Toronto Raptors.
Kuminga participated in the Rising Stars Challenge game for the 2022 NBA All-Star Game weekend.
At 19 years and 253 days, Kuminga became the second-youngest NBA champion after Darko Miličić.
On January 24, 2024, Kuminga scored 25 points on a perfect 11-for-11 from the field in a victory against the Atlanta Hawks.
This performance tied Chris Mullin's Warriors franchise record for the most made shots in a game without a miss.
In August 2022, Kuminga joined the DR Congo men's national basketball team for the African 2023 World Cup qualifiers.
Kuminga's older brother, Joel Ntambwe, played college basketball for UNLV before transferring to Texas Tech in 2019.
Two of Kuminga's cousins play professional basketball: Emmanuel Mudiay in Puerto Rico and Omari Gudul in Europe.
Kuminga's first language is French, and he is continuing to learn English.
